speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed that anyone else in your household or hotel room is experiencing similar itching or bumps? Additionally, have you recently started any new medications or supplements?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (infestation caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei).

Please note: Pyelonephritis is an infection of the kidney and would not present with intensely itchy red bumps on the thigh; your symptoms are classic for a parasitic infestation. Would you like me to request skin scraping images to confirm the diagnosis?
